10

Errors

Assertions, exceptions, and cleanup

Okanran: The Odù of Challenges

In Yoruba tradition, Okanran represents challenges and obstacles. In Ifá-Lang, the Okanran domain handles error handling, assertions, and exceptions.

Assertions (beeni / sise)

Use Okanran.beeni() to assert conditions are true:

Assertions 
ayanmo x = 42;

// Assert that x equals 42
Okanran.beeni(x == 42, "x should be 42");

// Assert that x is greater than 0
Okanran.sise(x > 0, "x must be positive");

Checking Conditions

Condition Checks 
Okanran.dogba(a, b);           // assert equal
Okanran.yato(a, b);            // assert not equal
Okanran.beko(condition, msg);   // assert false
Okanran.ko_si(value, msg);     // assert null/nil

The ewo Keyword

Use ewo / assert for inline runtime assertions:

Inline Assertions 
ewo balance >= 0, "Balance must be positive";
ewo user != ofifo;

// Without message
ewo x > 0;

Try / Catch / Finally

Use gbiyanju / try blocks with gba / catch to handle errors:

Try / Catch 
gbiyanju {
    ayanmo result = 10 / 0;
    Irosu.fo("Result: " + result);
} gba (err) {
    Irosu.fo("Caught error: " + err);
} nipari {
    Irosu.fo("This always runs");
}
try {
    let result = 10 / 0;
    Irosu.println("Result: " + result);
} catch (err) {
    Irosu.println("Caught error: " + err);
} finally {
    Irosu.println("This always runs");
}

Throwing Errors

Use Okanran.ta() or the ta / throw keyword to raise an error:

Throwing 
isodale divide(a, b) {
    ti (b == 0) {
        ta "Cannot divide by zero";
    }
    a / b
}

gbiyanju {
    ayanmo result = divide(10, 0);
} gba (err) {
    Irosu.fo("Error: " + err);
}
fn divide(a, b) {
    if (b == 0) {
        throw "Cannot divide by zero";
    }
    a / b
}

try {
    let result = divide(10, 0);
} catch (err) {
    Irosu.println("Error: " + err);
}

Deferred Cleanup

Use defer / gbe to schedule cleanup code that runs when the current scope exits:

Defer 
defer {
    Irosu.fo("Cleaning up...");
}

Irosu.fo("Doing work...");
// "Cleaning up..." runs when this scope exits
defer {
    Irosu.println("Cleaning up...");
}

Irosu.println("Doing work...");
// "Cleaning up..." runs when this scope exits

Fallible Operations (gbiyanju)

Use Okanran.gbiyanju() to try an operation with a default fallback:

Try with Fallback 
// Try an operation, use fallback on failure
ayanmo result = Okanran.gbiyanju(
    { -> Odi.ka("maybe_exists.txt") },
    "default content"
);
Irosu.fo(result);  // file content or "default content"

Proverbs as Error Messages

Okanran includes Yoruba proverbs (Okanran.owe()) for meaningful error context:

Proverbs 
// Get a random Yoruba proverb
ayanmo proverb = Okanran.owe();
Irosu.fo(proverb);  // "Bi a ba nṣe ire, a ko nii ṣe ibi"
Note

Ifá-Lang provides multiple error handling strategies: assertions with Okanran.beeni(), inline checks with ewo, structured exceptions with try/catch/finally, cleanup with defer, and fallback with Okanran.gbiyanju(). Choose the approach that fits your use case.

What You Learned

  • Assertions: Okanran.beeni(), Okanran.sise()
  • Inline assertions with ewo / assert
  • Structured exception handling: gbiyanju/try, gba/catch, nipari/finally
  • Throwing errors with ta / throw
  • Deferred cleanup with defer / gbe
  • Fallible operations: Okanran.gbiyanju()
  • Proverbs: Okanran.owe()
